headline: A roadmap shared on X suggests Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and Qualcomm could use Intel's chip-packaging services between 2027 and 2029.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: it rests on an unofficial roadmap posted on X, and the outlet says it is an analyst projection, not an official customer list.
importance_line: If it proves right, it would give Intel's foundry business big customers and give AI chip makers an alternative to TSMC's packaging lines, but it is an unofficial projection and TSMC is expected to keep the lead in packaging maturity and yields through at least 2028.
summary: Notebookcheck reports on a roadmap posted on X and credited to GFHK that names Amazon, Google, Qualcomm, Microsoft and Nvidia as possible outside customers for Intel Foundry's advanced packaging (the step that joins several chips into one unit) from 2027 to 2029, for example Amazon's third-generation Trainium AI chips in the first half of 2027 and Nvidia's future Feynman GPUs. The outlet stresses that this is an analyst projection, not an official list of customers, and that the dates are not confirmed and may change with market conditions.
notes: Single-outlet report of an unofficial roadmap; no confirmation from Intel or the named companies in the article. Apple is absent from the list; AMD may look at Samsung Foundry instead.
